properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (full Pier 70 geometry restart, after a systematic pass found 9 of this site's other 'trusted' parcels were meaningfully wrong): re-measured programmatically instead of by eye, for consistency with the rest of this site -- isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) and extracted a clean rectangular contour (OpenCV) at pixel (1203,437)-(1401,682). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Result is close to (within ~5m of) the prior hand-read version -- this parcel's own corners were already read correctly; kept for methodological consistency across the site. Still overlaps 'Noonan Building' by ~2843 m2 -- an already-documented, expected overlap given Noonan's own low-confidence, directional-only placement.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. EXTENDED SOUTH 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's south edge fell ~11m short of the real sidewalk visible in satellite imagery, leaving a strip of unclaimed vacant land between the block and the street -- consistent with this site's known local scale error for parcels far from the transform's Illinois/Michigan St anchors (see Parcel E1's digitization_method for the same root cause). The diagram itself (Figure 6.4.2) shows this block's fill running right up to the street with no setback, so extended the two south vertices by 11m (measured via satellite pixel-color transition to the real sidewalk, 3 sample transects) to close the gap, matching the diagram's own convention rather than re-deriving the whole transform.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Commercial/life-science, 90 ft max / 6 stories per Figure 6.4.2. Current design (DES Architects + Grimshaw, ~356,000-365,000 GSF, for King Street Properties' life-science program) superseded an earlier (2019) Hacker Architects + Quezada Architecture mass-timber office design (~300,000-310,000 sf, billed as one of the largest CLT office buildings in North America) -- both designs are real, the mass-timber one was simply replaced, not fabricated. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
